title: Replayable shadow promote with lifecycle hooks and rollback playbook
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Introduces a replayable shadow-to-canary promotion flow with lifecycle hooks and a documented rollback playbook. Backwards-compatible: runtime fallbacks unchanged. Admins get new telemetry and a Playbook doc link.
description:
Context: Customers running staged rollouts requested a safe, auditable path to "replay" shadow traffic that previously exercised a model so the same traffic can be promoted to a canary lane for deterministic validation. This PR implements a replayable shadow-promote flow that binds a shadow snapshot (request set + deterministic ordering + optional session affinity) to a canary promotion, plus lifecycle hooks and an operator-oriented rollback playbook. Motivation: reduce flakiness in A/B experiments caused by non-repro request sampling and to provide an operator playbook for fast, safe rollbacks when paired metrics diverge.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds a ShadowReplay manager component that captures shadow trace snapshots, exports a compact replay artifact (ndjson of requests with hashed metadata), and exposes a promote endpoint that wires a replay artifact into an ephemeral canary lane. We add lifecycle hooks at four points (pre-replay-validation, pre-cutover, post-cutover-health-check, and tear-down) so integration tests and customer callbacks can run deterministically. We bundle an operator rollback playbook in docs and surface telemetry (prometheus counters + tracing tags) to ensure traceability and postmortem replayability. The implementation is non-invasive to existing runtime path: normal live traffic continues to use existing schedulers; replay runs are isolated to dedicated worker pools and cannot take autoscaling capacity reserved for live lanes unless explicitly allowed by admin policy.

Checklist:
- [x] Shadow snapshot schema and storage (compact ndjson)
- [x] Replay engine + deterministic ordering
- [x] Promote API and RBAC check
- [x] Lifecycle hook triggers + generic hook interface
- [x] Telemetry (metrics + tracing tags)
- [x] Operator rollback playbook (docs)
- [x] Unit + integration tests for happy and failure paths
- [x] E2E smoke on staging with sampled trace file

Commits (high-level):
- 1f4a2b0: add shadow snapshot schema, exporter, and storage adapter
- 2b9d5e1: implement ReplayEngine with deterministic ordering and session-affine routing toggle
- 3c7e9aa: add /promote-replay API, RBAC, and promo ACL checks
- 6d1b4f2: lifecycle hook wiring and hook interface + example hook (smoke validator)
- 8a7f3d9: telemetry: counters, histograms, tracing tags for replay flows
- 9e4b2c3: docs: operator rollback playbook and runbook examples
- a1b8c6f: tests: unit + integration + e2e smoke harness updates

Changed areas (high-level):
- runtime/shadow/replay_manager.go (new): snapshot capture and export logic
- runtime/shadow/replay_engine.go (new): deterministic replay runner and worker pool
- api/routers/promote_replay.go (new): HTTP endpoint + ACL checks
- orchestration/hooks.go (mod): lifecycle hook wiring and registry
- telemetry/metrics_replay.go (mod): replay-specific metrics and prefixes
- docs/runbooks/replay-playbook.md (new): operator playbook with rollback steps
- tests/integration/replay_flow_test.go (new): integration coverage for replay->promote->cutover
- deploy/helm/values.yaml (mod): expose replay worker pool config and RBAC toggles

Testing and CI notes: CI initially flagged a flaky integration test (replay ordering edge with concurrent KV cache hits). I added a deterministic test harness and retry logic in the worker pool; CI now passes. Perf benchmarks on staging show replay runs average 1.8x cost per-token vs live (expected due to emulated sequencing and extra validation hooks) and do not affect live traffic throughput because they run in a bounded worker pool.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature flag replay.enable (off by default).
2) Canary deploy replay manager to staging, run replay artifact from nightly smoke traces (tested already).
3) Opt-in a small set of customers (internal beta) with explicit admin opt-in and quota.
4) After 2 weeks of stable runs and no regressions, enable for all Dedicated customers behind a policy toggle.

Operator rollback playbook (summary):
- If promoted canary shows divergence in fidelity metrics (>5% delta in combined quality score or latency regressions >25th percentile), trigger: 
  - step 1: pause any further promotions (API call)
  - step 2: snapshot canary logs and export replay artifact for postmortem
  - step 3: revert routing to previous canary snapshot (atomic swap)
  - step 4: if rollback fails, quarantine canary lane and scale to zero (automated fail-safe)
  - step 5: file postmortem and schedule forensic replay using exported artifact

Backward compatibility: The feature is guarded by replay.enable and RBAC. Existing canary and shadow flows remain unchanged unless promoted by the new API.

Telemetry and observability: added metrics: replay.snapshot.created, replay.run.started, replay.run.success, replay.run.failed, replay.promote.attempts, replay.promote.duration_ms. Traces are tagged with replay_id and snapshot_hash for cross-service correlation. Dashboards: new Replay Promotes dashboard (staging) and alert rules for replay.run.failed > 5 in 10m.

Security and privacy: replay artifacts redact PII by default (configurable allowlist). Artifacts are encrypted at rest using existing KMS keys and expire automatically after 7 days unless retained by an investigation flag.

Notes and tradeoffs: Deterministic replays require capturing additional metadata (headers, session ids) which increases artifact size. We opted for a compact ndjson line-per-request format and optional payload truncation to keep artifacts small. Cost and storage are exposed as quotas in the admin console.

Related work: this builds on ENG-16239 (shadow capture pipeline) and references the session-affinity RFC (DES-54).

Next steps: expose a UI flow in Console for selecting a snapshot and promoting; add canary traffic shaping options during promote (gradual phasing).

Merge notes: squashed commit on merge; preserved author attribution in commit message.

review_discussion: Carlos Mendes (reviewer): Can the replay artifact be replayed across cluster restarts? Also please ensure encryption keys are rotated safely.

Priya Kapoor (author): The artifact includes a short checksum and uses snapshot_store which survives cluster restarts; KMS integration follows existing rotation policy (described in Security section).
Aisha Rahman (reviewer): We need a non-privileged view-only endpoint for SRE to inspect artifacts without ability to promote — add an RBAC role.
Priya Kapoor (author): Added promo.view role and updated helm values to configure roles. See commit 3c7e9aa.
Benji Liu (reviewer): Integration test initially flaked on concurrent KV cache access during replay; did you consider isolating cache for replay workers?
Priya Kapoor (author): Yes - replay worker pool uses a read-only cache snapshot and isolated write-path; detailed in replay_engine.go and integration test covers the race scenario.
Aisha Rahman (approver): Approved after doc updates and e2e smoke on staging.
